info.desc: Endtroducing..... is the debut studio album by American hip hop artist DJ Shadow. It was released on November 19, 1996 by Mo' Wax Records. The album was conceived as an effort by Shadow to make an album completely based around sampling. It is structured almost entirely out of sampled elements from genres ranging from hip hop, jazz, funk, psychedelia, as well as samples from films and interviews. All sampling on the album was done on an Akai MPC60 MKII sampler. DJ Shadow released Endtroducing..... when he was 24 years old. Frequenting record stores to find music, he would often bring .

podcast.body: DJ Shadow, an American artist and considered one of the pioneers of instrumental hip hop, oddly achieved initial success for *Endtroducing.....* in the United Kingdom, where he recorded it. The album was seen as electronic craftsmanship by the industry but had little impact outside the UK initially. It quickly gained recognition across Europe, but its appreciation in the United States was significantly delayed, taking a considerable amount of time before it was fully understood and recognized as a masterpiece. "A pesar de eso, Diezado sacaría su disco en Londres y no tuvo pradía en ningún éxito en Estados Unidos."

podcast.body: Released in 1996, DJ Shadow's album, "Introducing," marked a pivotal moment in music history by being the first record made entirely from fragments of old, existing discs. This pioneering work fundamentally changed the trajectory of electronic music and, in part, the entire history of music, establishing a new conceptual framework for composition.

podcast.body: The album includes fragments of songs by Björk, an artist explicitly mentioned as being credited within *Endtroducing.....*. This highlights that while many samples were from forgotten and uncredited sources, some identifiable and recognizable artists did have their work integrated and acknowledged. "hasta Vior, que está creído en el Entrodius, porque hay fragmentos de alguna canción de Vior."

podcast.body: The album is a complex collage of numerous forgotten and abandoned records that had never received attention. DJ Shadow spent years, often eight to ten hours a day, meticulously searching through "musical waste" in record stores to unearth these hidden gems. He resurrected hundreds of such discarded discs, incorporating them into his work. Many of these samples were never credited because their original artists, labels, or even existence were unknown or unregistered, making them impossible to trace or claim. "este disco de DJ se ha dado es un complejo colas de todos estos pequeños discos olvidados y abandonados que nunca le he sido caso."

srcs.episode: DJ SHADOW - Endtroducing... (la música con desechos)

podcast.body: This album is hailed as a monumental work and the first record to be recorded 100% using sampling processes. It was entirely created by taking fragments, cutting, pasting, and sampling existing records. It is considered to have inaugurated the "golden age of the DJ as an artist." "el primer disco de DJ Shado, el Introducing, que aparte de ser un grandísimo disco, es el primer disco grabado 100% con procesos de sampling."

This album is widely considered a historical landmark, described as a revolution upon its release, despite not inventing new techniques or methodologies in itself. Its profound significance lies in its contextual value, representing a creative culmination rather than a fresh start. DJ Shadow meticulously crafted the entire album using the Akai MPC60, processing abandoned records found during years of dedicated digging. It is officially cataloged as the first album made 100% through sampling processes, although this claim is subject to controversy due to varying definitions of sampling and the inclusion of some recorded elements like vocals. The album's production style, marked by manual imperfections and rhythmic breaks, solidified processes still in use over two decades later. "Posiblemente el disco de día y sado es el disco que termina todo el proceso de desarrollo musical del hip hop, como que a partir de ese disco conceptualmente el hip hop instrumental llega a un punto climax y a partir de ahí evoluciona muy poco."
